Outbound Technical Implementation

    • Business Rule: After Update rule on the incident table that triggers when state changes to 6 ("Escalated").
    • ServiceNow RESTMessageV2 (Outbound) — used to POST to the Jira endpoint.
  • Dependencies between records or functions:
    • The Business Rule depends on the Incident record being in state 6.
    • The Script Include depends on valid credentials being configured in ServiceNow.

  • Authentication method:
    • Basic Auth using an API Token for Jira Cloud access.

  • Validation steps:

    • Confirm the JSON payload includes number, short_description, description, and assignment_group.
    • Check that the HTTP response from Jira contains a valid key field (e.g., PROJ-123).
    • Ensure the u_jira_key field on the Incident record is updated with the returned Issue Key.

    3. Wait for the Business Rule to trigger the outbound REST call.
    4. Check the Incident record in ServiceNow for the populated u_jira_key field.
    5. Verify the corresponding issue exists in Jira Cloud.

Testing Guide

Overview / Summary

Content

  • This interface handles LDAP authentication requests for the Service Portal, specifically addressing intermittent SSO login failures caused by LDAP query timeouts under heavy load.
  • Developers and system administrators managing identity integration and SSO configurations.
  • LDAP authentication queries and connection status metrics.
  • The process flow involves an increased connection timeout, a custom retry mechanism via a Script Include, and continuous monitoring of connection status to prevent false "User Not Found" errors and unnecessary incident creation.

Inbound Technical Implementation

Content

  • LDAP_Retry_Authenticator: A custom Script Include using the GlideLDAP API that implements a do-while loop to attempt the LDAP search up to 3 times with a 500ms delay between attempts.
  • The authentication flow is configured to use the LDAP_Retry_Authenticator Script Include instead of the standard authentication logic.
  • No specific REST API endpoints are exposed; the logic is internal to the authentication flow.
  • The loop logic requires a maximum of 3 attempts and a 500ms delay parameter.
  • Flow: Authentication request received → LDAP_Retry_Authenticator initiates LDAP search → If timeout/failure, wait 500ms → Retry (up to 3 times) → If successful, proceed; if all retries fail, return friendly error message.
  • Validation: Verify that transient failures do not result in "User Not Found" errors after retries are exhausted, and that a friendly error message is displayed if the LDAP server remains unreachable.

Outbound Technical Implementation

Content

  • LDAP Server Record: The production LDAP Server record configuration was modified to increase the 'Connection Timeout' from 5 seconds to 15 seconds.
  • Scheduled Job: A scheduled job runs every 10 minutes to check the ldap_connection_status metric.
  • Email Alert Rule: Triggered by the scheduled job if issues are detected in the ldap_connection_status metric.
  • Event Rule Disabling: The standard event rule that automatically creates Incidents for login failures was disabled to prevent high-priority incidents from transient LDAP failures.
  • Dependencies: The scheduled job depends on the availability of the ldap_connection_status metric. The Email Alert depends on the scheduled job execution.
  • Authentication method: Standard LDAP authentication via the GlideLDAP API with increased timeout.
  • Validation: Monitor the scheduled job logs to ensure it checks the metric every 10 minutes and that Email Alerts are triggered correctly upon failure detection.

How to Use the Interface

Content

  • Typical usage scenario: A user attempts to log in to the Service Portal via SSO, and the system automatically applies the retry mechanism if the initial LDAP query times out or fails.
  • Step-by-step instructions:
    1. Ensure the production LDAP Server record has the 'Connection Timeout' set to 15 seconds.
    2. Verify the authentication flow is configured to use the LDAP_Retry_Authenticator Script Include.
    3. Confirm the standard event rule for auto-creating Incidents on login failures is disabled.
    4. Verify the scheduled job for checking ldap_connection_status is active and running every 10 minutes.
  • Expected results: Transient LDAP failures are retried up to 3 times. If the server is unreachable after retries, a friendly error message is shown. No high-priority incidents are created for transient failures. Alerts are sent if the connection status metric indicates issues.

Testing Guide

Content

  • Test scenarios:
    • Simulate LDAP server unavailability to trigger retries.
    • Verify that after 3 failed attempts, a friendly error message is displayed.
    • Confirm that no Incidents are created for transient login failures.
    • Test the scheduled job and Email Alert triggering mechanism.
  • Test data: Use a group of 50 mock users for testing, as done in QA validation.
  • Step-by-step testing instructions:
    1. Configure the LDAP server to simulate timeouts or unavailability.
    2. Attempt SSO login with test users.
    3. Observe the retry behavior in the logs (3 attempts, 500ms delay).
    4. Check for the friendly error message if all retries fail.
    5. Verify that no Incidents are created in the system for these failures.
    6. Manually trigger the scheduled job to test the ldap_connection_status check and Email Alert.
  • Expected results: 0 false negatives ("User Not Found" errors) for transient failures. Friendly error message works correctly. No automatic Incidents are created. Email Alerts are sent when the scheduled job detects issues.
  • Where to check logs:
    • System Logs for LDAP_Retry_Authenticator execution and retry attempts.
    • Scheduled Job logs for the ldap_connection_status check.
    • Email Alert logs for triggered alerts.

Known Issues

Content

  • Symptoms: Intermittent "User Not Found" errors during SSO login on the Service Portal, especially under heavy load.
  • Root causes: LDAP query timeouts due to the original 5-second connection timeout being too short for heavy load conditions, leading to false negatives in authentication.
  • Diagnostic steps:
    1. Check System Logs for LDAP timeout errors.
    2. Verify the ldap_connection_status metric via the scheduled job.
    3. Review the LDAP_Retry_Authenticator logs to confirm retry attempts were made.
  • Resolution / Workaround: The implemented retry mechanism and increased timeout resolve the issue. If the LDAP server is genuinely down, the friendly error message informs the user, and the Email Alert notifies the admin team.
  • Prevention: Regular monitoring of the ldap_connection_status metric and maintaining the increased timeout configuration. Ensure the retry Script Include is kept in the authentication flow.

Investigation Steps

Content

  • Quick, structured troubleshooting guide:
    • When to use this guide: When users report SSO login failures or when the ldap_connection_status metric triggers an Email Alert.
    • Step-by-step investigation flow:
      1. Check the ldap_connection_status metric value via the scheduled job logs or dashboard.
      2. Review System Logs for LDAP_Retry_Authenticator entries to see if retries were attempted and failed.
      3. Verify the LDAP Server record's 'Connection Timeout' is set to 15 seconds.
      4. Confirm the authentication flow is using the LDAP_Retry_Authenticator Script Include.
      5. Check if the standard event rule for auto-creating Incidents is disabled.
    • Where to check logs: System Logs, Scheduled Job logs, Email Alert logs.
    • Key components: LDAP_Retry_Authenticator Script Include, LDAP Server record, ldap_connection_status metric, Scheduled Job, Email Alert rule.
    • Escalation guide: If the LDAP server is unreachable after retries and monitoring confirms the issue, escalate to the Infrastructure Team to investigate the LDAP server status. If the retry logic is not working, escalate to the Integration Team to review the LDAP_Retry_Authenticator Script Include configuration.

Overview / Summary

This workflow automates the creation of Knowledge Base (KB) articles directly from completed ServiceNow Stories. When a Story reaches the Closed Complete state, developers can trigger a server-side UI Action that sends the Story's technical context to an external FastAPI service. The AI pipeline generates a formatted HTML KB article, saves it to the ServiceNow KB, and returns the link to the Story's work notes.

Key Components:

  • Custom Field: u_technical_specification on the rm_story table to capture deep technical context.
  • Script Include: SnowKbGenerator for REST API integration.
  • UI Action: Create KB Article on the rm_story form.
  • External Service: FastAPI endpoint at http://10.20.30.40:8000/generate-kb.

Outbound Technical Implementation

The integration uses native ServiceNow REST capabilities (sn_ws.RESTMessageV2) to communicate with an external FastAPI server. The flow is initiated server-side via a UI Action and handled by a Script Include.

1. Script Include: SnowKbGenerator

  • Purpose: Server-side utility to trigger KB article generation.
  • Configuration:
    • API_URL: http://10.20.30.40:8000/generate-kb
    • API_KEY: Configured in the initialize() method.
  • Functions:
    • generateKb(storyId, storySysId): Sends a POST request to the FastAPI endpoint with story_id and push: true. Uses a 60-second timeout. On success (HTTP 200), appends the generated KB URL and title to the work_notes field. On failure, logs the error to work_notes.
    • _addWorkNote(storySysId, note): Updates the work_notes field of the rm_story record. Includes try-catch to handle write failures gracefully.

2. UI Action: Create KB Article

  • Target Table: rm_story
  • Condition: Visible only when current.state == '3' (Closed Complete).
  • Implementation Details:
    • Payload: Sends story_id, push: true, and force_update: true to the FastAPI endpoint.
    • Timeout: 120 seconds (longer than the Script Include to accommodate AI generation time).
    • Error Handling:
      • HTTP 200: Updates work_notes with the KB URL and title.
      • HTTP 422 (Unprocessable Entity): Interprets as missing mandatory data (e.g., Assignment Group). Updates work_notes with the specific error detail and displays an error message to the user.
      • HTTP 409 (Conflict): Indicates a KB article already exists. Updates work_notes and displays an info message suggesting re-click to overwrite.
      • Other Errors: Logs HTTP status and response body snippet to work_notes and displays a generic error message.
    • Navigation: Sets redirect and return URLs to keep the user on the Story form after execution.

3. Data Exchange

  • Request: JSON payload containing story_id, push, and force_update.
  • Response: JSON containing kb_url and kb_title on success, or error details on failure.

How to Use the Interface

Prerequisites:

  • The Story must be in the Closed Complete state.
  • The u_technical_specification field should contain relevant technical context for better AI generation.

Steps:

  1. Navigate to the Story record in ServiceNow.
  2. Ensure the Story state is Closed Complete.
  3. Click the Create KB Article button in the UI Action menu.
  4. Wait for the process to complete (may take up to 120 seconds).
  5. Check the Work Notes section of the Story for the generated KB article link and title.

Expected Results:

  • Success: A new work note is added with the KB article URL and title. A success message is displayed.
  • Duplicate (HTTP 409): An info message indicates a KB article already exists. The user can re-click to overwrite.
  • Missing Data (HTTP 422): An error message specifies the missing data (e.g., Assignment Group). The work note contains the error detail.

Testing Guide

Test Scenarios:

  1. Successful Generation:
    • Test Data: A Story in Closed Complete state with valid u_technical_specification and assignment_group.
    • Steps: Click Create KB Article. Verify a new KB article is created and the link appears in work_notes.
    • Expected Result: HTTP 200 response. Work note added with KB URL.
  2. Duplicate Detection (HTTP 409):
    • Test Data: A Story that already has a KB article generated.
    • Steps: Click Create KB Article again.
    • Expected Result: HTTP 409 response. Info message displayed. Work note updated.
  3. Missing Data (HTTP 422):
    • Test Data: A Story in Closed Complete state with assignment_group cleared.
    • Steps: Click Create KB Article.
    • Expected Result: HTTP 422 response. Error message displayed specifying missing data. Work note updated with error detail.

Where to Check Logs:

  • Work Notes: On the Story record, check the work_notes field for success or error details.
  • System Logs: Check the syslog table for REST API call details and error stacks if issues occur.

Known Issues

1. Timeout Errors

  • Symptoms: UI Action fails with a timeout error.
  • Root Cause: AI generation takes longer than the 120-second timeout.
  • Resolution: Retry the action. If persistent, check the FastAPI service health and load.

2. Missing Assignment Group

  • Symptoms: HTTP 422 error with "missing mandatory data" message.
  • Root Cause: The Story's assignment_group field is empty.
  • Resolution: Assign a valid group to the Story and retry.

Investigation Steps

When to Use: When KB article generation fails or behaves unexpectedly.

Step-by-Step Investigation:

  1. Check Story State: Verify the Story is in Closed Complete state.
  2. Check Work Notes: Review the work_notes field for specific error messages (HTTP 409, 422, etc.).
  3. Verify Required Fields: Ensure assignment_group and u_technical_specification are populated.
  4. Check System Logs: Search syslog for errors related to SnowKbGenerator or the REST call to http://10.20.30.40:8000/generate-kb.
  5. Test External Service: Use a REST client to manually POST to the FastAPI endpoint with a valid story_id to verify the service is responsive.

Key Components:

  • Script Include: SnowKbGenerator
  • UI Action: Create KB Article
  • External Endpoint: http://10.20.30.40:8000/generate-kb

Escalation: If the issue persists after checking logs and external service health, escalate to the Integration Team with syslog excerpts and Story ID.

Overview / Summary

Content

  • What the interface is: A synchronization mechanism between ServiceNow Change Tasks (CTASKs) and SAP SolMan Change Documents (CDs) to ensure state consistency.
  • Who uses it: Developers and Integration Team members managing the SolMan-ServiceNow integration.
  • What type of data is exchanged: SolMan Change Document states (Confirmed, Withdrawn) mapped to ServiceNow Change Task states (Closed, state=3).
  • High-level process flow: When a SolMan CD reaches a terminal state, the linked ServiceNow CTASK is evaluated for closure. A Business Rule handles real-time updates, while a one-time Fix Script reconciles historical data inconsistencies.

Inbound Technical Implementation

Content

  • Script Includes and their functions:
    • Business Rule: SolMan: Sync CD State to CTASK Closure Readiness on the change_task table.
      • Trigger: Runs Before update.
      • Condition: u_cd_state.changesTo() == true.
      • Logic: If u_cd_state changes to Confirmed or Withdrawn, the script queries all sibling CTASKs linked to the same parent Change Request (chg_request). It auto-closes them (state=3) only if every sibling CTASK has a terminal CD state.
    • Fix Script: SolMan: Fix CD State Inconsistencies.
      • Execution: One-time Scheduled Script Execution in non-production.
      • Logic: Identifies CTASKs where u_cd_state is in (Confirmed, Withdrawn) and state is not 3. It verifies the parent Change Request has no active CTASKs with non-terminal states, then updates qualifying CTASKs to state=3.
  • Required parameters:
    • u_cd_state: Must be Confirmed or Withdrawn.
    • parent: Link to the parent Change Request to identify sibling tasks.
  • Flow and its steps:
    1. SolMan updates the CD state to a terminal state.
    2. ServiceNow updates the u_cd_state field on the linked CTASK.
    3. The Business Rule fires on update.
    4. The rule checks if the new state is terminal.
    5. If terminal, it checks all sibling CTASKs for the same parent CHG.
    6. If all siblings are in terminal states, all are set to state=3.
  • Validation steps:
    • Verify the Business Rule condition u_cd_state.changesTo() == true is active.
    • Confirm that closure only occurs when all sibling CTASKs have terminal CD states.

How to Use the Interface

Content

  • Typical usage scenarios:
    • Real-time synchronization when a SolMan CD is confirmed or withdrawn.
    • One-time reconciliation of historical data inconsistencies in non-production environments.
  • Step-by-step instructions:
    1. For Real-Time Sync: Ensure the Business Rule SolMan: Sync CD State to CTASK Closure Readiness is active on the change_task table. No manual action is required; the rule triggers automatically upon u_cd_state update.
    2. For Historical Reconciliation:
      1. Access the Scheduled Script Execution module in a non-production instance.
      2. Execute the script SolMan: Fix CD State Inconsistencies.
      3. Review the log output to validate the count and correctness of updated records.
      4. Promote the fix to production only after validation in non-prod.
  • Expected results:
    • CTASKs linked to terminal SolMan CDs are automatically closed (state=3).
    • Historical orphaned CTASKs are reconciled and closed if all sibling tasks are in terminal states.
    • Log output confirms the number of records updated.

Testing Guide

Content

  • Test scenarios:
    • Single CTASK linked to a CD changing to Confirmed.
    • Multiple sibling CTASKs where one changes to Withdrawn and others are already Confirmed.
    • Multiple sibling CTASKs where one changes to Confirmed but another is still in a non-terminal state (e.g., In Progress).
    • Execution of the Fix Script on a dataset with known inconsistencies.
  • Test data:
    • Create a parent Change Request with two linked CTASKs.
    • Set u_cd_state for both to non-terminal values initially.
    • Update one to Confirmed and verify no closure occurs.
    • Update the second to Withdrawn and verify both close.
  • Step-by-step testing instructions:
    1. Create test Change Request and linked CTASKs in a non-production instance.
    2. Simulate SolMan state updates by changing u_cd_state on CTASKs.
    3. Observe the Business Rule behavior: Ensure CTASKs do not close until all siblings are in terminal states.
    4. Execute SolMan: Fix CD State Inconsistencies on a set of records with historical mismatches.
    5. Check the log output for the number of records updated.
    6. Verify that only CTASKs with terminal u_cd_state and no active sibling tasks were closed.
  • Expected results:
    • CTASKs remain open if any sibling has a non-terminal CD state.
    • CTASKs close (state=3) only when all siblings have terminal CD states.
    • Fix Script log shows accurate counts of updated records.
  • Where to check logs:
    • Scheduled Script Execution log for the Fix Script output.
    • System Logs for Business Rule execution details if debugging is required.

Known Issues

Content

  • Symptoms:
    • CTASKs remain open (state != 3) even though their linked SolMan CD is Confirmed or Withdrawn.
    • Inconsistency between SolMan CD state and ServiceNow CTASK state.
  • Root causes:
    • Historical data inconsistencies due to previous lack of automated closure logic.
    • Manual updates to u_cd_state that did not trigger the Business Rule correctly.
  • Diagnostic steps:
    • Check the u_cd_state and state fields on the CTASK.
    • Verify if the Business Rule SolMan: Sync CD State to CTASK Closure Readiness is active.
    • Check if all sibling CTASKs for the parent CHG have terminal CD states.
  • Resolution / Workaround:
    • Execute the SolMan: Fix CD State Inconsistencies script in non-production to reconcile historical data.
    • Ensure the Business Rule is active for future real-time synchronization.
  • Prevention:
    • Monitor the Business Rule execution logs for errors.
    • Regularly audit CTASKs with terminal u_cd_state but non-closed state to detect new inconsistencies early.

Investigation Steps

Content

  • Quick, structured troubleshooting guide:
    • When to use this guide:
      • When a CTASK is not closing despite its SolMan CD being in a terminal state.
      • When data inconsistencies are reported between ServiceNow and SolMan.

      1. Identify the CTASK in question and note its u_cd_state and state.

      3. Verify the u_cd_state of all sibling CTASKs. If any are non-terminal, the current CTASK should not have closed.
      4. If all siblings are terminal but the CTASK is still open, check the Business Rule SolMan: Sync CD State to CTASK Closure Readiness for errors or deactivation.

Overview / Summary

Content

  • What the interface is: An inbound SOAP integration where the ALMEX SAP system acts as the client and ServiceNow acts as the SOAP server. It automates the repair order workflow for ALMEX devices by allowing ALMEX to query and update repair request data within ServiceNow.
  • Who uses it: Stores (via ServiceNow Service Catalog) to submit repair requests, and the ALMEX SAP system (via SOAP calls) to process and track those requests.
  • What type of data is exchanged: Repair order details including device serial numbers, parcel tracking information, and status updates. The serial number serves as the primary ID in ALMEX, while ServiceNow uses the Requested Item sys_id and number for correlation.
  • High-level process flow:
    • A store user submits a request via the "ALMEX Customer Repair Request" catalog item.
    • A Flow sets the correlation_id and correlation_display fields on the catalog item to link it with the ALMEX serial number.
    • ALMEX periodically calls the ServiceNow SOAP endpoint to read open requests (GetReturns) or update/close them (ConfirmReturns).
    • ServiceNow returns the relevant data based on the configured field mapping.

Inbound Technical Implementation

Content

  • Script Includes and their functions:
    • ALDIAlmexInterface: Contains the core logic for the two SOAP operations: GetReturns and ConfirmReturns. The trigger condition is "ALMEX -> SN".
    • ALDIAlmexInterfaceClient: Provides support functions, including handling reference qualifiers and reading system properties required for the catalog item processing.
  • Scripted Web Service and Endpoints:
    • A Scripted Web Service named ALDIAlmex defines the inbound endpoint.
    • A Static WSDL named ALDIAlmex defines the SOAP contract expected by the ALMEX system. This is used because ALMEX expects a standard SOAP contract rather than a ServiceNow-generated WSDL.
  • Required Parameters & Configuration:
    • System Properties:
      • aldi.integration.almex.config: Holds global integration settings.
      • aldi.almex.config.list: Defines country-specific rules, such as whether a VAT ID is required for a specific country.
      • aldi.integration.almex.config.matrix: Defines the SOAP response layout and maps ServiceNow catalog item fields to the ALMEX response payload.
    • Integration User: interface.almex.user is configured with the snc_internal role and all necessary SOAP roles (excluding delete permissions).
  • Flow and its steps:
    • Flow Name: "Cat Item: ALMEX Customer Repair Order"
    • Action: Automatically sets the correlation_id and correlation_display fields on the catalog item. This allows the system to use the Requested Item sys_id and number in responses without needing to access unique ALMEX variables like the serial number directly in the response logic.
  • Validation Steps:
    • Catalog Client Scripts handle request validation and loading of default data when a store user submits the "ALMEX Customer Repair Request" item.

How to Use the Interface

Content

  • Typical usage scenarios:
    • A store receives a defective ALMEX device and needs to send it for repair.
    • The store user creates a service request in ServiceNow to track the repair process.
  • Step-by-step instructions:
    1. Navigate to the Service Catalog in ServiceNow.
    2. Select the catalog item ALMEX Customer Repair Request.
    3. Enter the device serial number and other required details. The Catalog Client Scripts will validate the input and load default data based on the country/VAT settings in aldi.almex.config.list.
    4. Submit the request. The Flow "Cat Item: ALMEX Customer Repair Order" will automatically populate the correlation fields.
    5. Wait for the ALMEX system to poll the ServiceNow endpoint. ALMEX will retrieve the request via the GetReturns operation.
    6. As the repair progresses, ALMEX will update the status or close the request via the ConfirmReturns operation, which will reflect in ServiceNow.
  • Expected results:
    • The repair request is visible in ServiceNow with correct correlation IDs.
    • Status updates from ALMEX (e.g., parcel tracking, repair completion) are synchronized back to the ServiceNow record.

Testing Guide

Content

  • Test scenarios:
    • Create a new "ALMEX Customer Repair Request" and verify that the Flow correctly sets correlation_id and correlation_display.
    • Simulate an ALMEX GetReturns call to ensure the open request is returned with the correct field mapping from aldi.integration.almex.config.matrix.
    • Simulate an ALMEX ConfirmReturns call to update the status or close the request in ServiceNow.
    • Verify that the Integration User interface.almex.user has the correct permissions to perform these actions.
  • Test data:
    • Valid ALMEX device serial numbers.
    • Country codes configured in aldi.almex.config.list to test VAT ID requirement logic.
  • Step-by-step testing instructions:
    1. In a non-production environment, create a test user with the snc_internal role.
    2. Submit a test catalog item for "ALMEX Customer Repair Request".
    3. Check the record to confirm the correlation fields are populated.
    4. Use a SOAP client (e.g., SoapUI) to send a GetReturns request to the ALDIAlmex endpoint using the ALDIAlmex WSDL.
    5. Verify the response payload contains the expected fields mapped from the catalog item.
    6. Send a ConfirmReturns request to update the status.
    7. Verify the status change in ServiceNow.
  • Expected results:
    • Successful SOAP responses with no authentication or mapping errors.
    • Correct data synchronization between ServiceNow and the ALMEX test system.
  • Where to check logs:
    • System Logs > All > SOAP Web Services to monitor inbound calls and errors.
    • System Logs > All > Script Includes to check for errors in ALDIAlmexInterface or ALDIAlmexInterfaceClient.

Known Issues

Content

  • Symptoms:
    • Recording function issues after release changes (noted in technical specification).
    • Potential mismatch in field mapping if the aldi.integration.almex.config.matrix system property is not updated when catalog item fields change.
  • Root causes:
    • The catalog item consists of almost 70 objects, which can complicate update set management.
    • Static WSDL and System Properties must be manually kept in sync with the ALMEX system's expectations.
  • Diagnostic steps:
    • Verify that the aldi.integration.almex.config.matrix property matches the current catalog item fields.
    • Check SOAP logs for specific error codes related to WSDL parsing or authentication.
  • Resolution / Workaround:
    • Ensure all update sets (STRY0429735_V2, STRY0429735_V3) are applied correctly to cover adjustments made after preview/UAT.
    • Manually verify the System Properties after any catalog item changes.
  • Prevention:
    • Include a review step in the deployment checklist to verify System Properties and WSDL alignment.

Investigation Steps

Content

  • Quick, structured troubleshooting guide:
    • When to use this guide: When ALMEX reports failed SOAP calls, or when ServiceNow records are not updating as expected after ALMEX interactions.
    • Step-by-step investigation flow:
      1. Check the System Logs > SOAP Web Services for the specific timestamp of the failed call. Look for authentication errors (401/403) or parsing errors (400).
      2. If authentication fails, verify that the interface.almex.user account is active and has the snc_internal and required SOAP roles.
      3. If parsing fails, compare the incoming SOAP request against the ALDIAlmex Static WSDL. Ensure the ALMEX system is sending the expected format.
      4. If data is missing or incorrect in the response, check the aldi.integration.almex.config.matrix system property to ensure the field mappings are correct.
      5. If the correlation ID is missing on the catalog item, check the Flow "Cat Item: ALMEX Customer Repair Order" to ensure it executed successfully.
    • Where to check logs:
      • System Logs > All > SOAP Web Services: For inbound request/response details.
      • System Logs > All > Script Includes: For errors in ALDIAlmexInterface or ALDIAlmexInterfaceClient.
      • System Logs > All > Flows: To verify the execution of the "Cat Item: ALMEX Customer Repair Order" flow.
    • Key components:
      • Scripted Web Service: ALDIAlmex
      • Script Includes: ALDIAlmexInterface, ALDIAlmexInterfaceClient
      • System Properties: aldi.integration.almex.config, aldi.almex.config.list, aldi.integration.almex.config.matrix
      • Integration User: interface.almex.user
    • Escalation guide:
      • If the issue persists after verifying logs and configuration, escalate to the Integration Team for further analysis of the SOAP contract or ALMEX-side issues.
